title: Cross-Environment IAM Provenance and Retention Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook captures a single-source approach for IAM event provenance (who changed what, when, why) and retention policies across Redwood's three hosting tiers (hosted, dedicated, private). The goal is to ensure auditability, meet regulatory retention requirements, and provide deterministic evidence artifacts for automated audits and SIEM correlation.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: security engineers, compliance, SREs, platform engineering, and support leads.
- Scope: RBAC v2 changes (role edits, role bindings, privilege escalations), credential lifecycle events (creation, rotation, revocation), deployment-time access changes (canary rollouts, emergency fastpaths), and system-initiated fallback actions.

Design principles (high level):
1) Immutable provenance: every change must map to an immutable audit event with a unique event_id and cryptographic hash where possible.
2) Environment-aware retention: retention TTLs differ by hosting tier and regulatory profile.
3) Evidence-first automation: on high-risk events, collect evidence snapshots (policy version, active bindings, recent token issues) automatically and attach to the event record.
4) SIEM-friendly enrichment: events exported to SIEM should include normalized fields and static schema to avoid field churn.

Core fields for audit_log schema (required for all events):
- event_id: stable UUID4 string
- timestamp_utc: RFC3339 timestamp
- actor: principal id (user:alice or svc:deploy-bot)
- actor_type: user|service|system
- actor_ip: ip or null
- action: high-level verb (role.create|role.update|role.bind|cred.issue|cred.revoke|policy.attach|policy.detach|env.escalate)
- target_type: role|policy|credential|tenant|org|route
- target_id: canonical identifier for target
- before_snapshot_hash: SHA256 hex or null
- after_snapshot_hash: SHA256 hex or null
- change_summary: short human summary (max 200 chars)
- justification_id: id for attestation/evidence or null
- evidence_refs: list of artifact ids (see evidence automation)

Enrichment fields (recommended):
- deployment_mode: hosted|dedicated|private
- region: cloud region code
- trace_id: request trace linking to runtime traces
- request_payload_digest: SHA256 of action payload

Retention matrix (baseline recommendations):
- Hosted (standard customers): audit events: 2 years; high-risk events (privilege escalation, external data access): 7 years; evidence artifacts: 7 years
- Dedicated (enterprise customers with contract): default to contract retention but minimum 3 years for audit events; high-risk: 7 years; evidence artifacts: per contract
- Private (customer-managed): provide local export tools and a retention policy template; platform stores only provenance pointers and short-term evidence (90 days) unless contractual SLA requires otherwise

Note: retention must be configurable per-tenant for Dedicated and Hosted (compliance flags).

RBAC v2: role taxonomy (recommended minimal set for cross-env mapping)
- org-admin: org-level configuration, cannot access customer PII by default
- env-admin: full environment control (deployments, infra); scoped per environment
- tenant-admin: tenant-scoped role with ability to manage tenant settings and keys
- svc-infer: service role used by inference workers (least privilege for model load / KV access)
- audit-reader: read-only access to audit indices and evidence artifacts
- escalation-approver: can approve emergency role activations (requires 2FA + attestation)

Role-binding patterns by environment (quick rules):
- Hosted: no org-admin cross-tenant role bindings; env-admins are Redwood internal SRE/ops principals. Tenant-admins are customer principals bound to tenant namespace. Every binding must reference justification_id.
- Dedicated: env-admin may be customer or Redwood depending on contract. All admin bindings require periodic attestation (90 days) and automated evidence snapshot at attestation time.
- Private: primary model is customer-managed; Redwood support accounts may have ephemeral access via ephemeral-privilege activation flow (see below). Evidence export hooks must be present locally.

Policy template snippets (JSON-like pseudo-policy; treat as template snippets to be parameterized):
- Least-privilege service role (svc-infer):
  {
    "role_name": "svc-infer",
    "permissions": [
      "model:read",
      "kv:read:prefix:models/active",
      "cache:use",
      "logging:write:inference-metrics"
    ],
    "constraints": {
      "network_sources": ["10.0.0.0/8","internal-redwood-prod"],
      "time_window": "none",
      "max_token_generation": "200k/day"
    }
  }

- Emergency escalation fastpath (approval required):
  {
    "role_name": "temp-privilege-elevate",
    "ttl": "2h",
    "approval": {
      "approvers": ["escalation-approver"],
      "multi_factor_required": true,
      "justification_required": true
    },
    "audit_hook": "collect_evidence_snapshot()"
  }

Evidence automation flow (high level):
1) Trigger (events that cause collection): role.bind to high-privilege roles, cred.issue for long-lived keys, env.escalate, or manual attestation
2) Collector lambda (or cloud function) runs with read-only elevated service principal. It gathers:
   - current role definition (JSON)
   - active bindings for the role (list)
   - last 72h login events for principals bound
   - last 30d token issue events referencing the principals
   - deployment manifests if relevant (to tie code changes)
3) Hash and store artifacts in evidence storage (immutable blob store) with retention metadata and signed metadata file (artifact_id, hash, created_by)
4) Attach artifact_id to the originating audit event and push to SIEM

Automation pseudocode (shell + curl example):
- Collect snapshot:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $COLLECTOR_TOKEN" \
    "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/roles/$ROLE_ID/snapshot?includeBindings=true" \
    | jq . > /tmp/role-snapshot.json
  sha256sum /tmp/role-snapshot.json > /tmp/role-snapshot.sha256
  upload_tool put /tmp/role-snapshot.json --tags event_id=$EVENT_ID --ttl=7y

SIEM export mapping (normalized field set for ingestion):
- host_field: event_host (string)
- ts_field: timestamp_utc (rfc3339)
- id_field: event_id
- user_field: actor
- actor_type
- action
- resource_type: target_type
- resource_id: target_id
- change_digest: request_payload_digest
- evidence_links: evidence_refs (array -> flattened CSV for SIEM)
- severity: derived (low|med|high) - high if action in [env.escalate, cred.issue long-lived, role.bind to org-admin]
Examples: Splunk HEC ingest considerations
- Put event_id and trace_id fields at top level to support dedup and correlation
- Use evidence_refs as a JSON array in a dedicated field (avoid free-text concatenation)
- Include signed_snapshot_hash as 'snapshot_hash' so the SOC can verify integrity

Evidence access patterns for audits:
- Read RFC: auditors should receive time-limited read URLs and an integrity manifest signed by platform KMS. The manifest lists artifact ids, their hashes, and a chain-of-trust (who requested the snapshot, who collected it).

Ephemeral access (private deployments) workflow (recommended):
- Request: support engineer opens an ephemeral access request via the support portal (Jira ticket created automatically)
- Approval: two approvers (customer security contact + Redwood escalation-approver) must approve in UI or via signed SAML assertion
- Activation: system issues short-lived credentials (1h), records provisioning event, collector takes immediate evidence snapshot and attaches it to the ticket
- Postmortem: after session ends, an automated session recording digest and command summary is attached to the artifact and included in post-access attestation

Operational runbooks (quick checks):
- Detect: alert on sudden burst of role.bind events (>10 in 5m) or role.create for org-admin
- Contain: automatically revoke temp-privilege-elevate if detected outside business hours without two approvers
- Remediate: rotate any long-lived keys that were recently issued by a principal that had a failed attestation

Checklist for onboarding a new tenant to retention & provenance policy:
- [ ] Capture tenant-specific retention requirement and add to contract metadata
- [ ] Enable evidence automation collector for tenant namespace
- [ ] Verify SIEM export mapping and field compatibility with customer SIEM
- [ ] Run a dry-run that triggers several evidence snapshots and validate manifest signatures

Appendix A — Minimal attestation template (short):
- attestation_id: ATTEST-2024-xxxx
- attested_by: escalation-approver or security lead
- attested_on: 2024-11-05T14:22:00Z
- scope: role.bind events for tenant-1234
- verdict: approved|revoked|needs_followup
- notes: free text (<=1000 chars)

Appendix B — Quick reference: field lengths and types
- event_id: 36 chars UUID4
- timestamp_utc: RFC3339
- actor: <=128 chars
- change_summary: <=200 chars
- evidence_refs: list of artifact ids, each <=64 chars

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should private deployments have an optional escrowed evidence storage (encrypted by customer key) managed by Redwood? Pros: easier centralized audits. Cons: additional compliance surface.
- Default retention: confirm whether legal requires 7 years for hosted high-risk events or if we can set 5 years in certain geos.

Next steps (owners):
- Security: finalize schema with SIEM team and ship conversion library (GO/Python) (owner: Ethan Park)
- Platform: implement collector lambda and signed-manifest support (owner: Lucia Moreno)
- Legal: confirm retention minimums for EU/US APAC contracts (owner: Daniel Cho)

Notes to reviewers: this is a working playbook intended to be referenced by the SIEM export guide and the RBAC v2 specification. Recommend cross-team review before changing retention numbers.
